title: Automatic substitution playbook for version locks: graceful substitution, health windows, and telemetry contracts
creator: Sana Patel
description: Problem statement: Customers can pin models/versions to guarantee output stability, but production incidents, regional capacity shortages, and model deprecations require a controlled, observable automatic substitution mechanism that preserves contractual SLAs and avoids silent regressions. This ticket defines a playbook and implementation constraints for automatic substitution of pinned versions at different failure modes: health-window substitution, regional surge substitution, and deprecation-driven migration. Focus areas include business rules for when to substitute, compatibility checks, grace periods, operator overrides, telemetry surface, and rollback semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic policy engine exists that can evaluate requests for pinned versions and decide substitution actions according to configured rules
Substitution modes implemented: soft-substitute (retry to compatible variant), regional-shift (route to cross-region equivalent), and deprecation-evict (scheduled replacement after notice period)
Compatibility validator runs pre-flight on candidate substitutes and rejects substitutions that change schema/structured-output expectations
All substitutions emit standardized telemetry events and trace spans consumed by Console and alerts when substitution rate exceeds thresholds
A canary rollout of substitution logic with a 0.1% sample is supported, with automatic rollback on quality degradation metrics
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design the policy DSL and state machine for substitution decisions; add unit tests for compatibility checks. Phase 2: Implement a policy evaluator microservice integrated with routing layer; extend model metadata with compatibility fingerprints and golden_prompt checks. Phase 3: Telemetry contracts and Console hooks; add guardrails for operator overrides and manual hold. Phase 4: End-to-end e2e and chaos tests; prepare runbook and launch playbook. Implementation details: use existing runtime fallback API to route to candidate variants, but require a pre-flight compatibility probe that validates tokenization, function-calling schema, and sample prompts from customer-owned prompt sets before any automated substitution is accepted.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged build behind org-level opt-in. 2) Internal canary: route 0.1% of requests across non-production orgs; monitor latency, cost per token, and QA tests against golden prompts. 3) Customer internal beta with explicit opt-in and notification of grace window. 4) Gradual ramp (0.1 -> 1 -> 5 -> 25%) with automated pause if substitution_quality_drop > 2% or substitution_rate > configured threshold. 5) General availability with default conservative rules and an admin console panel to inspect substitution traces.
telemetry_requirements: Emit substitution.decide event with fields: reason, selected_variant, fallback_path, preflight_result, policy_id
Emit substitution.outcome event with fields: success|reverted|blocked, latency delta, token delta
New dashboard in Console: per-tenant substitution rate, per-policy error rate, per-variant performance delta, and recent substitution traces
Alerting: paged alert when substitution_rate > 0.5% of total traffic for an org AND substitution_quality_drop > 1% over 15m
Retention: substitution traces must be retained for 30 days for debugging and 90 days for compliance customers
risks_mitigation: Risk: silent quality regressions. Mitigation: pre-flight compatibility checks using customer prompt set and golden metric comparisons before accepting automated substitution
Risk: cascading cross-region load. Mitigation: quota-aware regional broker that enforces capacity limits and back-pressure into policy decisions
Risk: operator error when deprecating a version. Mitigation: deprecation is a two-step process (announce -> soft-window -> hard-evict) with automatic rollback and issuer confirmations
Risk: telemetry gaps leading to incomplete incident triage. Mitigation: define mandatory telemetry contract and fail-fast if the contract schema is not present
